newsitem.title: FRANCE: French maize price firms as rain disrupts harvest.
newsitem.headline: French maize price firms as rain disrupts harvest.

text.p: Prompt delivery maize prices firmed on Tuesday as heavy rain held up combining of early variety maize in France's southwestern and eastern regions, threatening to disrupt port deliveries, dealers said.
FOB Rhine maize for delivery this week fetched 1,010-1,020 francs per tonne against 990 francs on Monday.
FOB Atlantic maize for delivery this week was offered at 1,030 francs per tonne -- a premium of 30 francs over deliveries for next week and 110 francs over end of the month deliveries.
Operators said commitments to deliver the grain by the end of the week may be particularly hard to honour if the poor weather conditions lingered.

"Anxiety levels are rising," one dealer said, adding three ships were already waiting in the port of Bordeaux to load some 10,000 tonnes of maize. Further vessels were expected in the southwestern port in coming days.
Rouen wheat for October-November delivery was quoted at 880-885 francs per tonne and Rouen barley for October-December delivery at 860-870 francs per tonne, unchanged from Monday.
MATIF wheat futures were very quiet with only the September 1997 expiry quoted at 879 francs, down two on Monday. Volume was a thin five lots in mid-afternoon trading.
